Subject: Inference throughput degradation impacting /api/v1/generate

Hi Mateo,

We started seeing a sharp increase in errors and latency around 14:30 PDT when our production traffic hit the reserved pool. Summary:
- p95 latency jumped from ~1.8s to ~8s over the last 20 minutes
- 5xx error rate climbed to ~4.8% (mostly 503/504)
- Our token/QPS usage is within our committed reservation but the responses are timing out

This is customer-facing — several merchants are backing off. Can you confirm this is due to restricted headroom on your dedicated GPU pool vs a model-level regression? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can provide temporary burst capacity or fallback to a compatible hosted variant.

Attaching a short CSV with request counts and sample 5xx traces.

Thanks — we’re standing by for a bridge.

— Daniel

Irene / Marissa / Vivek — looping you in. Quick notes from initial checks: 
- Telemetry shows a sustained queue buildup in the dedicated pool for tenant CLR-78932 beginning ~14:20 PDT. KV-cache hit rates look normal.
- Kernel-selection and GPU telemetry do not indicate an OOM; instead we’re seeing high scheduling latency on the pool (likely noisy neighbor / insufficient burst headroom).
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/XYZ/clearstream-overview (included in thread)

Immediate proposal:
1) Approve a one-time emergency burst (add 2x short-lived GPUs to their pool for the next 60 minutes) to relieve queueing and reduce p95.
2) Open a 30-min triage bridge (CS + Eng + Customer ops) — I can be on the call.
3) If agreed, enable fallback routing for their critical route to a compatible hosted variant with slightly different model profile while we stabilize.

Customer is asking for an ETA and whether we’ll grant burst credits vs applying usage-based charges. If we can push a short-lived capacity increase now we should avoid SLA breach / retention risk. I’ve attached logs_summary.csv with the sample traces Daniel shared.

Quoted message below.
